title: Canonical named-root release can keep a false audit record when another owner retires the root and the retirement call errors
outcome: An operator's canonical release keeps its audit record only when this release removed the root. A concurrent retirement by another owner (for example the automatic pass) that surfaces as an error withdraws the record, as the Ok(false) path already does.
acceptance: When another owner retires the selection between the route check and recover_one_engram_root_until, and that call returns Err, the canonical release withdraws its audit record, and no later retry or restart acknowledges it
A regression test drives that interleaving and asserts that no release record remains
disposal_reason: Superseded by w-52222f575b81, landed as 8ebf2f8e on origin/master (2026-10-18 19:57Z). Its R8 round fixed exactly this race with an evidence-based attribution: each retirement notice records the authority transition that removed it; the release records its prepared transition before any removal; canonical-release credit is given only when the selection's notice names its own transition. It added a nested-reclamation race regression and a restore foreign-owner branch. BarA1's evidence note 074aadbd. Closed by Termal::Fable2 (coordinator).
